reason: Melting a sample seems like the first step toward separating the solid grains, and it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the selected ice sample to melt, leaving its brown material in water for filtering, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Melting released the particles but erased their original positions, so I can examine the grains while the remaining sample stays preserved.
reaction: The loss of positional information is a useful and slightly surprising tradeoff.
reason: Filtering seems like the natural way to separate the suspended solids, and it is the only gameplay combination offered.
expectation: I expect the cloth to retain the brown grains while the meltwater passes through, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The filter separated the solids, but they are crowded together; the next goal is to examine them closely.
reaction: The crowded filter makes me curious about what the microscope can distinguish.
reason: The microscope is the natural tool for examining the trapped particles, and this is the only gameplay combination offered.
expectation: I expect to see details of the trapped grains, though I do not know what features will be visible.

effect: The microscope revealed a segmented body with limbs, partly damaged on the filter. That makes preserving the remaining ice without melting it a new priority.
reaction: I was surprised by the body, and the damaged side made the earlier loss of context feel consequential.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the membrane was most worthwhile: the unexpected body gave the sampling process a compelling consequence and raised a question about what remains in the ice.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filtering was physically clear but offered little decision-making, since it was the only gameplay combination available.

surprise.text: The jointed, segmented body surprised me; I had expected to see grains rather than something with limbs.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: melting, filtering and microscopy each had a clear purpose, although each was the only gameplay combination offered.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to learn whether the unbroken ice contains a whole specimen and what can be learned from it.
